newsitem.title: UK: Gold tightly rangebound, PGMs edgy.
newsitem.headline: Gold tightly rangebound, PGMs edgy.

text.p: Gold prices are trading in an increasingly narrow $340-$346 range, but the market could be gearing up for a breakout, analysts said.
The more volatile platinum group metals (PGM), meanwhile, are closely watching Russia-Japan supply talks for direction.

GOLD - With the focus of the precious metals complex concentrated on platinum and palladium, gold has been tethered to a relatively narrow range in recent weeks. But it may be getting ready to break out, analysts said.
"The coiling is getting tighter and tighter within the limits. I would expect is to start moving shortly," said analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Market sentiment is being swayed by developments in Germany's plan to revalue gold reserves and signs that European Monetary Union may be delayed.
But traders are also wary that forward selling by Australian gold producers could soon pressure the market.
At 0900 GMT spot gold was indicated at $344.00/$344.40, compared to Monday's New York close of $343.30/$343.80.
SILVER - The market is clearly rangebound in a $4.60-$4.92 band, and needs to break above the top end of the band to negate any downside bias, Jones said.
At 0900 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.74/$4.76, up three cents from Monday's late close.
PLATINUM/PALLADIUM - Both markets are extremely volatile within thin volumes, and will remain so until the Russian-Japanese supply saga comes to a close, analysts said.

"Palladium has had a major reversal in the past few days. It got up to $202 and then came back to major support at $165," Jones said, adding that $162 was a key support level for the white metal. Palladium was last at $180.00/$184.00, up nearly $10.
Platinum, meanwhile, should find good support in the $385-$390 area.
Platinum was last indicated at $403.00/$406.00, compared to $399.50/$402.50 at the previous late close.
